claims.label: The process begins when a customer reports a card transaction they believe is incorrect or unauthorised.
Receive the report through an approved channel and confirm the customer’s identity using the channel’s authentication procedure.
Locate the relevant card account and transaction using approved systems.
Create a unique dispute case ID and record the date and time received, channel, customer identifier, and officer handling the case.
Capture the customer’s description in their own words where practical, including why the transaction is disputed and when they first noticed it.
Confirm whether the customer recognises the merchant, location, amount, date, and transaction type without leading the customer toward a particular answer.
Check whether a related fraud report, previous dispute, merchant refund, reversal, or open case already exists.
Assign a provisional dispute category based on the customer’s account and available transaction information.
Determine whether the transaction is pending, posted, reversed, refunded, or otherwise not yet eligible for the requested dispute route.
Check the applicable customer terms, card-scheme requirements, legal obligations, and internal procedures for time limits and required evidence.
Assign case priority according to risk, time remaining before a deadline, customer impact, and internal service targets.
Route potential fraud or account compromise to the appropriate team while retaining ownership or a tracked hand-off.
Retrieve the transaction from the approved card-processing or core banking system.
Confirm whether it is authorised, posted, reversed, refunded, disputed previously, or linked to another transaction.
Compare the transaction date, amount, currency, merchant information, and reference with the customer’s account.
Review relevant available records for the transaction channel, such as chip/contactless, online, wallet, ATM, or other approved channel data.
Check whether merchant credits, reversals, partial refunds, or currency-conversion differences explain the reported issue.
Record findings, sources consulted, and any limitations in the case notes.
Confirm that the transaction and dispute category qualify for the proposed remedy.
Confirm the case is within the applicable time limit or identify an authorised exception route if one exists.
Check that mandatory evidence and customer declarations are present.
Review any merchant response, previous credit, reversal, partial refund, or duplicate case to prevent double recovery.
Calculate the proposed amount and determine whether the case is full, partial, or not eligible.
Write a concise recommendation with supporting facts, applicable rule reference, risks, and unresolved questions.
Confirm the case meets the institution’s provisional-credit criteria, if applicable.
Calculate the amount based on the eligible disputed transaction and any prior refunds or reversals.
Obtain the required approval and create the credit through the approved system.
Clearly record whether the credit is provisional or final, the posting reference, and any conditions for reversal.
Track the case until a final decision determines whether further adjustment is required.
Confirm that the case is approved for submission and all required fields and evidence are complete.
Select the correct reason/category and required code in the authorised platform, using current authoritative guidance.
Attach evidence in the accepted format and verify that documents are legible and relevant.
Submit before the applicable deadline and capture the platform/network reference and timestamp.
Confirm that the platform accepted the submission; if the status is uncertain, investigate before retrying to avoid duplicate submissions.
Update the case status, next expected action, and follow-up date.
Review the case queue for approaching deadlines, outstanding evidence, and responses due from external parties.
Record incoming responses and documents promptly, linking them to the correct case.
Assess whether new evidence changes eligibility, the recommended outcome, or the amount.
Escalate missed service targets, deadline risks, and unresolved platform issues to the designated supervisor.
Maintain customer updates at the frequency required by policy and applicable service commitments.
Confirm the final decision and any required approval.
Check whether a provisional credit, merchant refund, reversal, or previous adjustment has already been posted.
Calculate the net amount due to or from the customer, avoiding duplicate credits or recoveries.
Post the authorised adjustment through the approved system and retain the posting reference.
Reconcile the adjustment to the dispute record and transaction ledger.
The process ends when the case is resolved, any required adjustment is posted, the customer is informed, and the record is closed or transferred to a controlled recovery process.
